security_privacy_cost_impact: None to access: no grant, policy or read surface changes. Operational: a parent DELETE/UPDATE no longer scans a child table under the parent's lock on twelve keys, and the next key added without an index fails migrate-clean by name instead of waiting for a large table.
migration_and_data_impact: Eleven CREATE INDEX statements (SHARE lock for the build; every table empty on every instance this batch reaches; on a populated instance the recovery is CONCURRENTLY per statement outside a transaction, which the driver's one-transaction apply does not do -- stated in the file, as 131 did).
compatibility_impact: None. run.mjs exports two new symbols (FK_SUPPORT_EXEMPTIONS, FK_SUPPORT_PROBE_SQL); the migrate-clean target gains one probe line of output.
known_limitations: The four exemptions rest on the referenced ids being globally unique; if a later batch makes a subscription or invoice id per-workspace, the exemption is wrong and the reason beside it says which fact it rests on.
The rule accepts a partial index only on one of the key's own columns IS NOT NULL; a partial on any other predicate is not support, by design.
open_risks_or_blockers: None opened; blocker 162 (no FK-index lint; twenty-one keys) is re-headed CLOSED.
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert the merge commit: the eleven indexes, the probe and the rule go; the blocker reopens as it was.
recommended_next_work_packages: The apply-time silencing class (Q0 P6: `false and` / `return;` inside a do-block) as one static rule over every migration.
The closure generator into the tree (scripts/db/gen-closure.mjs) with a regenerate-and-diff test.
reviewer_instructions: Remove 104 from the set on a scratch PostgreSQL and run migrate-clean: the probe must name the twelve keys.
Add a fictitious key to FK_SUPPORT_EXEMPTIONS and run migrate-clean: it must be refused as stale.
Read each of the four exemption reasons against the index it names (pg_indexes) and decide whether the fact it rests on holds.
